segments.text: Verse one. From Surah Ta-Ha. And Adam disobeyed his Lord.
وَعَصَى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ
First, the verb. Disobeyed. It is a past verb, so it is fixed.
The wa before it means and. It is a particle. It never changes.
Who disobeyed?
آدَمُ
Adam. He is the doer, so he takes rafʿ, with damma.
Only one damma, no tanween. Some names never take tanween.
Whom did he disobey?
رَبَّهُ
His Lord. That is the object, so it takes naṣb. Its sign is fatha.
His is an attached pronoun at the end of the word. It is the owner, and it is fixed.
Because Lord is owned, it has no tanween. Just one fatha.
Listen to the verse once more.
وَعَصَى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ
Verse two. From Surah Hud. And Nuh called out to his son.
وَنَادَى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ
First, the verb. Called out. It is a past verb, so it is fixed.
The wa before it is a particle. It never changes.
Who called out?
نُوحٌ
Nuh. He is the doer, so he takes rafʿ, with damma.
This name does take tanween. Damma with tanween.
Whom did he call?
ابْنَهُ
His son. In English we say called out to his son. The Arabic has no extra word.
So it is the object. It takes naṣb. Its sign is fatha.
His is the attached pronoun. It is the owner, and it is fixed.
Son is owned, so no tanween. Just one fatha.
Verse three. From Surah An-Naml. And Sulayman inherited from Dawud.
وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَانُ دَاوُودَ
First, the verb. Inherited. It is a past verb, so it is fixed.
The wa before it is a particle. It never changes.
Who inherited?
سُلَيْمَانُ
Sulayman. He is the doer, so he takes rafʿ, with damma.
Only one damma. This name never takes tanween.
Whom did he inherit from?
دَاوُودَ
Dawud. In English we say from Dawud. The Arabic has no extra word.
He is the object, so he takes naṣb, with fatha.
Only one fatha. Like Adam, this name never takes tanween.
